agree.reason: A quick-reading committee member gets a clear, specific case: he runs the 3 a.m. milking alone, flags sick cows using the herd software, and caught nine mastitis cases early, and the letter takes on his weak written English directly, so most readers would rank him favourably.

honest.reason: Several claims go beyond the brief: 'nobody asked' him to learn the software, 'with no formal training', 'communicates clearly with me, our crew and our vet', and 'seriously ill'; it also leaves out the five-week absence and the two days' notice by calling it 'one family emergency'.

works_the_facts.reason: It uses the facts as given but derives nothing from them: two missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled (about 99.7% attendance) is never worked out, and the nine mastitis cases are never tied to milk or cost saved.

right_comparison.reason: It compares him with others only through the vague 'one of the people I would most like to see get this training' and gives no measure of how he stands against other workers or applicants.

qualification.reason: The English caveat is honest and names a remedy (the night class), but the reader cannot check anything: there is no course level, no end date and no measure of progress.

objections.reason: The two likely objections, written English and reliability, are met head-on, though the long absence is softened rather than squarely addressed.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager, with sensible bold section leads and placeholders, which matches what the brief asked for.
